clue.text: Impeach criminal, European smuggling New Zealand animal

indicators.note: to smuggle something is to carry it hidden inside, so one piece is tucked within the rest
a criminal act is a crooked one, so the letters of impeach are bent into a new order

parts.note: the letters of impeach are used as written

explanation.surface: A demand that some European offender who sneaked goods in from New Zealand be put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impeach criminal' reads as a call to arms, but criminal is the anagram signal for the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimpanzee is a great ape, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Intimidates Conservative Members of Parliament, not Labour initially

indicators.note: not says the letter that follows is left out of the word

parts.note: a parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls, so its members are owls

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Labour

parts.note: the party name supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: Tories bully MPs, but the Labour lot are spared.
explanation.walkthrough: Members of Parliament look like politicians; the setter means birds, since a 'parliament' is a flock of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, a synonym of intimidate.

clue.text: Upset, admit Phil's on air regularly being tasteless

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so they read from the bottom
regularly takes every second letter of the phrase, at a steady interval

parts.note: the phrase supplies its second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone is told to concede that Phil's broadcast performance was bland.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of 'admit Phil's on air' and they spell the answer backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or talk lacks flavour or interest, a close synonym of tasteless.

clue.text: Rain spoilt trip to Nice, pair ultimately conceded

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: these words are used as written

indicators.note: conceded means given up; ultimately says it is the last letter of pair that goes

parts.note: the word pair is used as written before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A couple's holiday on the Riviera was ruined by bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rain' looks like the cause of the spoilt trip, yet it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation is the meteorologist's word for rain, snow and hail falling from the sky.

clue.text: Bother Greek character with one's naked dances

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
one is I, and 's stands for is

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so dances loses its outer letters

parts.note: dances stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Greek lad has a problem with his nude dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is a source of annoyance, and bother as a noun means just that sort of irritation.

clue.text: Escape from crazed avengeful revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the hidden letters read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of crazed and the start of avengeful

explanation.surface: Someone flees a wild, vengeful rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to slip away from or avoid capture, a verb synonym of escape.

clue.text: Guzzling whiskey, flipping drunk couples

indicators.note: a guzzler takes something in, so the outer word swallows the letter
flipping turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pairs of revellers are knocking back whisky and getting thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word qualifying drunk; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Twos are sets of two, so the word works as a synonym for pairs or couples.

clue.text: Cheerful, with success certain

parts.note: a win is a success
certain, as in 'certain people', means some

explanation.surface: Someone is upbeat, being assured of victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming and engaging, and in older use bright or cheerful.

clue.text: Period before Spring in state of enchantment

indicators.note: before puts the first piece in front of the second, which suits a down clue read top to bottom

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: A season before spring seems magical.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like the season, but it is the verb meaning leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spellbound is held as if by magic, completely captivated.

clue.text: Fritter wife consumed, welcoming seconds

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: ate is the past tense of eat, meaning consumed

explanation.surface: A wife scoffed a fritter and then had second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: Fritter looks like the deep-fried snack, but it is the verb meaning squander.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money or time is to squander it, a verb synonym of waste.

clue.text: Home loan ahead of time

parts.note: in means at home
an advance is money lent ahead of payment

explanation.surface: A mortgage is arranged before it is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in advance means doing it beforehand, early.

clue.text: Rival occasionally angry after winner gets award

indicators.note: after says the alternating letters and angry come after the winner

parts.note: a victor is the winner

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some of the letters, every other one

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of Rival
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A sore loser fumes as the champion collects the prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military decoration for gallantry.

clue.text: Tommy's relaxed reportedly finding place to study

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Tommy is a British private soldier, so Tommy's is private's, and relaxed is cool: private's cool

explanation.surface: A British soldier is calm, apparently, about finding somewhere to read.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the old nickname for a British private; 'private's cool' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private school is a fee-paying institution where pupils go to learn.

clue.text: Usual person charged admits switching vehicle certificate

indicators.note: admits lets something in, so the outer word takes the other inside

parts.note: the accused is the person charged in court

indicators.note: switching rearranges the order of the letters

parts.note: an MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test certificate for a vehicle

explanation.surface: A defendant confesses to swapping a car's paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is the British annual test a car must pass; its certificate is called an MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed as in 'his accustomed seat' means customary or habitual.

clue.text: Purchase from fishmonger perhaps in fellow's pouch

definitions.meaning: first sense, read as two words
second sense: the flap worn over a man's crotch in old breeches

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as COD PIECE and it is something bought at a fish counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a bag or flap covering the groin in Renaissance menswear.

clue.text: Furore involving bottleneck essentially in Spanish city

indicators.note: involving means including, so the core letters sit inside

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or furore

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: a ten-letter word, so its essence is its two central letters

explanation.surface: Uproar over a traffic jam in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, once its capital.

clue.text: Unimportant matter in half-hearted midday publication

indicators.note: half-hearted loses half of the word's heart, one of its two middle letters

parts.note: noon is midday
an issue is an edition of a publication

explanation.surface: A trivial point appears in a feeble lunchtime edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-issue is something that does not matter, of no real concern.

clue.text: Remove cover fielder finally, man you told must keep back

indicators.note: back says the whole lot reads in reverse
must keep means the outer letters hold the fielder's last letter inside

parts.note: a chess piece is called a man, and a pawn is one

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of fielder

parts.note: the last letter of fielder

indicators.note: told means as said out loud, so the word is heard as a letter

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: the fielder at the end must hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: Man here is a chess piece, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap is to take the wrapping or covering off something.

clue.text: Extremely tedious argument over editor's material

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned over, read from the bottom up
extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of tedious
a row is an argument
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A dull dispute about an editor's copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Material looks like an editor's written copy; it is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted is a smooth woollen yarn and the fabric woven from it.

clue.text: Some of those tweeting about Cambridge college

parts.note: robins are some of the birds that tweet
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sample of social media users discuss a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeting' points to social media, but it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson College is the youngest undergraduate college of the University of Cambridge.

clue.text: One doubts it's PC somehow going on about energy cuts

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the letter sits inside
going on means being added next, so about follows
somehow says the letters come in some other order

parts.note: these letters are used as written, ignoring the apostrophe
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A doubter grumbles that political correctness keeps rambling about energy cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is a person who questions or disbelieves, someone doubting by habit.

clue.text: Extent of maybe cabby's manoeuvres around becoming cleric?

definitions.meaning: first sense: the smallest circle a vehicle such as a taxi can turn in
second sense, read cryptically: a circle being turned around becomes cleric

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a reverse anagram: turning the letters of circle gives cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning circle is the space a vehicle needs to make a U-turn; London taxis are famous for a tight one.

clue.text: Young environmentalist

definitions.meaning: first sense: ... as in inexperienced or immature
second sense: a member of an environmental party

explanation.definitionFit: Green covers both a raw novice and someone who campaigns for ecological causes.

clue.text: Left stunned at first following huge defeat

indicators.note: following says the first letter comes after the others

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for very large

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of stunned

parts.note: the opening letter of stunned

explanation.surface: A team is left reeling after a heavy beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a defeat in a match or contest.

clue.text: Rebels resume working to receive money

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the money goes inside
working means being worked over, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters of resume are used as written
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Strikers go back to work after getting paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Resume looks like the verb, but its letters are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutineers are people who rise in revolt against authority, especially on a ship.

clue.text: Best garden party?

definitions.meaning: first sense: to best someone is to beat or surpass them
second sense, read whimsically: a party held outside

explanation.walkthrough: A garden party is a do held out of doors, an 'out do'; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass them, and best as a verb means to beat.

clue.text: Princess has treat for queen

parts.note: Di was Diana, Princess of Wales
a do is a party or treat

explanation.surface: A princess enjoys a party thrown in a monarch's honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founding Queen of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas.

clue.text: Meets groups east of Bury

indicators.note: east of in an across clue means to the right, after

parts.note: to inter is to bury
sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: A gathering of factions just east of the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is capitalised to look like the town near Manchester; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that intersect cross each other, so they meet.
